lines.say: Nearly fifty thousand men were killed or wounded here. In a single day.
lines.cap: Nearly 50,000 men were killed or wounded here. In a single day.

lines.say: Napoleon had escaped from exile and taken back France. Now he needed one big win.
lines.cap: Napoleon had escaped from exile and taken back France. Now he needed one big win.

lines.say: Against him stood the Duke of Wellington. And a Prussian army under Blooker was marching to join him.
lines.cap: Against him stood the Duke of Wellington. And a Prussian army under Blücher was marching to join him.

lines.say: But it had rained all night. Napoleon waited for the mud to dry, and lost hours he would never get back.
lines.cap: But it had rained all night. Napoleon waited for the mud to dry, and lost hours he would never get back.

lines.say: His cavalry charged the British squares again and again. Not one square broke.
lines.cap: His cavalry charged the British squares again and again. Not one square broke.

lines.say: Then, in the afternoon, the Prussians slammed into his flank.
lines.cap: Then, in the afternoon, the Prussians slammed into his flank.

lines.say: Napoleon sent in his last reserve. The Imperial Guard. They marched up the ridge, straight into a wall of musket fire.
lines.cap: Napoleon sent in his last reserve. The Imperial Guard. They marched up the ridge, straight into a wall of musket fire.

lines.say: And a cry spread through the French army. The Guard is retreating!
lines.cap: And a cry spread through the French army: "The Guard is retreating!"

lines.say: Four days later, Napoleon gave up his throne. He died in exile, on Saint Helena.
lines.cap: Four days later, Napoleon gave up his throne. He died in exile, on Saint Helena.

lines.say: So who really won Waterloo? Wellington, or Blooker?
lines.cap: So who really won Waterloo? Wellington, or Blücher?
